body.p: . include/sxml/xquery.h is new; serialize.h grows by new constants at the end of sxml_serialization_method and new fields in sxml_serialization_parameters, regrouped by size (enumerations, presence flags, views) because clang-tidy's padding check rejects the interleaved order. Callers initialize by field name, so Phase 1 and 2 code compiles unchanged (zero is still the adaptive method with its defaults); nothing is ABI-stable before 0.2.0 ().

item.p: Methods: XML, XHTML, HTML, TEXT, JSON, CSV after ADAPTIVE. No constant for implementation-defined (namespaced) methods; the readers raise SEPM0016 for them. A method not implemented yet returns UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE (the header's contract); src/serialize.c still returns INVALID_ARGUMENT for non-adaptive methods until 3.3 changes it.

Parameters: one struct with every Serialization 4.0 parameter, including the 4.0 additions (canonical, csv-, escape-solidus, indent-unit, indent-attributes, json-lines, line-ending), field names the parameter names with _. Booleans are sxml_serialization_flag (DEFAULT, NO, YES), because several defaults are "yes" (escape-solidus, escape-uri-attributes, include-content-type, omit-xml-declaration) and a zero struct must mean "defaults"; DEFAULT is fn:serialize's default (F&O 4.0 table), so omit-xml-declaration defaults to yes; XSLT sets NO itself. Enumerations have their default as constant 0 (UTF-8, standalone omit, normalization none, LF, json-node-output-method xml). Parameters the spec lets be absent (doctype-, html-version, indent-unit, item-separator, media-type, version) are has_ + text; html-version stays text (an xs:decimal lexical form) because the HTML method also falls back on version. csv-separator and csv-quote-character are codepoints, 0 the default. Element-name lists are name pool identifiers (sxml_element_name_view, in serialize.h because name.h is frozen); character maps are codepoint/replacement pairs. Encodings: UTF-8, UTF-16 (big endian), US-ASCII, ISO-8859-1 (sxml_character_encoding); other names SESU0007. Indent unit default two spaces.

Errors: a value Serialization 4.0 does not permit is SEPM0016 (a dynamic error) when serialized, so fn:serialize sees the spec code; what XDM cannot even express (ill-formed UTF-8, unknown constants, name 0, a repeated character-map codepoint) is INVALID_ARGUMENT.

Parameter reader: sxml_serialization_parameter_reader (lifecycle quintet; allocator and item heap) reads fn:serialize's $options (empty, a map, or an output:serialization-parameters element) into the struct and owns the copied text and lists until its next read. Map: XPTY0004 for wrong types, SEPM0016 for bad values; element: SEPM0017, SEPM0018, SEPM0019 (Serialization 4.0, 3.1); method xml when none is given. The textual forms of XQuery output declarations and xsl:output (yes/no/1/0, \t, QName lists) are read by internal code of 3.10 and Phase 4, not by a public function.

XQuery: sxml_xquery_query (quintet, like sxml_xpath_expression; the main module's text is , glossary) compiled with the shared sxml_static_context_configuration, evaluated with sxml_xquery_evaluation_request holding the shared dynamic context. Host variable declarations are in scope in the main module only (a prolog declaration of the same name is XQST0049); bindings also bind every module's external variables. Library modules come from the resolver, kind XQUERY_MODULE, one request per location hint (an empty uri_reference for none); the parameter document of output:parameter-document is an XML_DOCUMENT request, read at compile time (XQST0119/XQST0115). Output declaration errors (XQST0108-0110, SEPM0016) are compile errors. sxml_xquery_query_get_serialization_parameters returns the struct by value: declarations over the parameter document over XQuery defaults (method xml); the host overrides fields of the copy (CLI --method).

Left out, each a later field: XQuery-only static context settings from the host (boundary-space, construction, ordering), a list of the query's external variables, fn:load-xquery-module options (3.11 is internal), implementation-defined serialization parameters.
